title: Ops Resilience: First Signs
description: Unusual power fluctuations across Singapore's grid. The readings don't match any known fault pattern. DIS suspects a sophisticated cyber intrusion into critical infrastructure.
storyContext: It starts with a flicker. Power readings from substations across Singapore spike and dip in a pattern that doesn't match any known fault. Your team pulls up the grid monitoring feed and the room goes quiet. Too coordinated to be coincidence. Someone is inside the control systems.

software-engineer.title: Set Up the Early Warning System
software-engineer.instruction: Deploy monitoring sensors across the power grid's control systems to catch the intrusion before it escalates. Arrange the steps.
software-engineer.hint: You can't spot unusual behaviour without knowing what normal looks like. Establish a baseline first, then set your tripwires.

items.label: Map all control system devices and how they connect to each other
Install monitoring sensors on each control system device
Record 2 hours of normal behaviour as a baseline
Set alert levels based on the baseline — anything unusual triggers a warning
Connect alerts to the security team for instant notification

data-scientist.title: Estimate How Far It Has Spread
data-scientist.instruction: The intrusion may have been active for days. The graph shows the percentage of devices flagging unusual activity across four monitoring windows. If the trend continues, how many of the 200 control devices may already be compromised?
data-scientist.hint: The percentage is climbing. Project the next value in the trend, then apply that percentage to the 200 total devices.

cloud-engineer.title: Deploy the Detection Toolkit
cloud-engineer.instruction: The readings don't match anything in the records. Your team needs the right detection tools to classify this threat before leadership responds. What approach?
cloud-engineer.hint: New threats are tricky for systems trained only on known patterns. Multiple methods combined tend to be more reliable than one fast method alone.

options.label: Run it through the automated threat detector. Answer in 5 minutes, but it was only trained on known attack patterns and this one looks new.
Manually compare the pattern against past incidents and intelligence reports. Takes 30 minutes but produces a high-confidence answer.
Run three different detection methods and go with the majority verdict. Slower than one alone, but much more reliable against something new.
Share the pattern with partner cybersecurity teams. Could get an answer in 10 minutes, but you'd be showing your hand to external parties.
